job.title: Senior Backend Engineer
job.rawText:
# Senior Backend Engineer

**Northwind Commerce** — Bengaluru, India · Hybrid

We are hiring a Senior Backend Engineer to own the services behind our checkout
and payments platform. You will design APIs, model data, and operate what you
ship in production.

## Requirements

- At least 5 years of professional backend development experience
- Strong Java
- Production experience with Spring Boot
- Designing and building REST APIs
- PostgreSQL, including schema design and query optimisation
- Docker

## Preferred

- Kubernetes in production
- AWS
- Kafka or another event-streaming platform
- CI/CD pipelines

candidates.name: Aman Verma
candidates.headline: Software Engineer · Java/Spring application development
candidates.aiSummary: Aman Verma is listed as a Software Engineer and has six months of internship experience fixing bugs in a Java monolith and writing unit tests, plus a Spring Boot/Docker university capstone. The resume does not evidence five years of backend work, production Spring Boot, REST API design, PostgreSQL schema or query optimisation, production Kubernetes, event streaming, or CI/CD; AWS, Kubernetes, and PostgreSQL appear only in the Skills list.

candidates.name: Neha Kapoor
candidates.headline: Senior Backend Engineer · Restaurant Discovery
candidates.aiSummary: Neha Kapoor has seven years of backend experience at Zomato, with demonstrated Python/Django, REST APIs, PostgreSQL optimisation, Docker, production Kubernetes, and AWS infrastructure work. The resume shows only one year of Java and does not demonstrate strong Java depth, production Spring Boot, Kafka or another event-streaming platform, or CI/CD pipeline work.

candidates.name: Priya Sharma
candidates.headline: Senior Backend Engineer · Fintech
candidates.aiSummary: Priya Sharma has eight years of evidenced backend experience, including six years building Java and Spring Boot payment services and earlier Java and Spring work at Freecharge. The resume evidences REST APIs, PostgreSQL schema and query optimization, Docker, AWS, Kafka, and GitHub Actions; it does not demonstrate Kubernetes, and it does not explicitly state schema design or CI/CD maintenance.

candidates.name: Rahul Das
candidates.headline: Backend Engineer · Food delivery
candidates.aiSummary: Rahul Das is a Backend Engineer with five years of Java backend experience at Swiggy, including production Spring Boot microservices, REST APIs, PostgreSQL, Docker, and AWS deployment. The resume does not demonstrate Kubernetes, Kafka or another event-streaming platform, or CI/CD, and it mentions PostgreSQL modelling and querying without explicit schema design or query optimisation.

candidates.name: Vikram Reddy
candidates.headline: Software Engineer · Cloud-native donations platform
candidates.aiSummary: Vikram Reddy has three years of professional software engineering experience at Ketto, working on cloud-native Java and microservices applications and REST API development for a donations platform. The resume does not evidence five years of backend experience, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, event streaming, or CI/CD, and it does not establish the depth of Java or REST API design experience.

questions.question: Your resume shows Spring Boot use in a university capstone project. What experience have you had deploying and maintaining Spring Boot applications in a production environment, and what responsibilities did you personally own after deployment?
questions.rationale: The capstone establishes familiarity with Spring Boot but not whether the candidate has operated it in production.
questions.followUp: Can you describe one Spring Boot service that real users depended on, including its deployment environment, an operational issue you handled, and how you resolved it?

questions.question: Your resume shows that you built an application with Spring Boot. Describe the REST APIs you designed and implemented for that application, including how you defined the resources and contracts and handled validation, errors, security, and testing.
questions.rationale: The application demonstrates Spring Boot development but does not establish explicit REST API design and implementation experience.
questions.followUp: Choose one endpoint you personally built and walk through its request and response contract, implementation, and the design decisions behind it.

questions.question: PostgreSQL is listed in your skills. Tell me about a project or role where you used PostgreSQL, focusing on how you designed the schema and how you investigated and optimised query performance.
questions.rationale: The skills list names PostgreSQL but provides no evidence of hands-on schema design or query optimisation.
questions.followUp: Can you give a concrete example of a slow query or database performance problem you improved, including the diagnosis, changes made, and measurable result?

questions.question: Kubernetes is listed in your skills. Describe the systems where you used Kubernetes in production, including what was deployed, the cluster environment, and your responsibilities for releases, configuration, scaling, monitoring, and incident response.
questions.rationale: The skills list does not establish that the candidate has used Kubernetes to operate production workloads.
questions.followUp: Describe a production deployment or Kubernetes incident you personally handled, including what you changed, how you validated the result, and how you would roll back if necessary.

questions.question: AWS is listed in your skills. Describe a professional or project system in which you used AWS, including the services involved, how the system was deployed and operated, and which parts you personally implemented or maintained.
questions.rationale: The skills list names AWS but does not demonstrate hands-on use in a project or professional setting.
questions.followUp: Can you walk through one AWS workload end to end, explaining its architecture, access controls, monitoring, and a problem you personally diagnosed or resolved?

questions.question: What experience do you have using Kafka or another event-streaming platform, and what problem did it solve? Please describe the producers, consumers, message or event design, delivery behaviour, and how the system was operated or troubleshot.
questions.rationale: The resume contains no evidence of event-streaming experience, so this question tests both exposure and depth of implementation.

questions.followUp: Tell me about one pipeline you personally changed or repaired, what was failing or needed improvement, how you diagnosed it, and what outcome resulted.

interviews.question: Your resume describes containerisation and cloud deployment; did you use Kubernetes in a production environment, and if so, walk me through the system, your responsibilities, and how you operated and supported it over time.
interviews.answer: Yes. At Swiggy I deployed our order services on AWS EKS. I owned the Helm charts, configured liveness and readiness probes, and set CPU and memory requests and limits. I ran the rolling deployments myself, and during one production incident a bad rollout was failing health checks, so I rolled it back with kubectl and then added a stricter readiness gate so it could not happen again. I was on the on-call rotation for that cluster for about a year.
interviews.reason: The recorded answer provides specific evidence of production Kubernetes use: the candidate deployed order services on AWS EKS, owned Helm charts and health checks, operated rolling deployments, resolved a production rollout incident by rolling back with kubectl, and supported the cluster on call for about a year.

evidence.quote: Yes. At Swiggy I deployed our order services on AWS EKS. I owned the Helm charts, configured liveness and readiness probes, and set CPU and memory requests and limits. I ran the rolling deployments myself, and during one production incident a bad rollout was failing health checks, so I rolled it back with kubectl and then added a stricter readiness gate so it could not happen again. I was on the on-call rotation for that cluster for about a year.
